findings.title: Stale duplicate test file committed
findings.description: This is a second copy of the pre-change `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`. The diff shows the same blob (`e6539010`), and it still calls `createContextPipeline(path)` with one argument. Its `.test.ts-E` name doesn't match a `*.test.ts` pattern, so it isn't the suite's file, and it will drift from the real one. Delete it.

findings.title: Adoption errors other than `AdoptionError` become a returned error stub
findings.description: The comment at `ContextIntegrator.ts:146-147` says adoption errors "propagate", and the `readAdoptionState` docstring says a malformed TOML "propagates the parser's error". Only `AdoptionError` is rethrown (line 123). A malformed `.context-forge.toml` makes `ConfigManager.readToml` throw the raw smol-toml error (`ConfigManager.ts:24-29`). The catch turns that into `getErrorContext`, and `cf build` (`build.ts:85`, `99-104`) puts the stub in its output without checking it, with no thrown error. The test "keeps the error-stub behavior for any other resolver error" (`ContextIntegrator.test.ts:434`) locks this in. Either rethrow resolver failures, or change the comment and docstring to describe what actually happens.

findings.title: Explicit-instruction match is case-sensitive; every other path is not
findings.description: `explicit` uses `instruction === BROWNFIELD_ADOPTION_INSTRUCTION`. `resolvePhaseValue` lowercases (`projectSchema.ts:161`). The `--it` flag (`build.ts:35-36`) and the MCP `instruction` field (`contextTools.ts:112`) are both free-form strings. So `Brownfield-Adoption` returns `selected: false` here. The build still gets the brownfield prompt and profile, because `SystemPromptParser.ts:188` and `ContextProfileParser.ts:178-180` are case-insensitive. The result is that the spelling `Brownfield-Adoption` skips the guide check and the Adoption Facts section, while `brownfield-adoption` gets both. Lowercase the value once and compare that.

findings.title: Catch-and-rethrow without logging
findings.description: `persistInProgress` wraps the write failure in an `AdoptionError` and rethrows without logging. CLAUDE.md requires an ERROR-level log before a re-raise, or a specific, commented case. The message carries the detail, so the user can see it, but the rule isn't met. `ContextIntegrator.ts:121-123` has the same gap for both rethrows. The existing `PermissivenessFragmentError` path does too, so fix the pattern once.

findings.title: Parity test re-implements the CLI path rather than running it
findings.description: The header says the CLI path runs "as build.ts does it", but the test builds `workingCopy` by hand and calls `createContextPipeline(..., 'persist')` itself. It skips `resolveProjectWorktree`, `ensureGuideReady`, the `--phase` and `--it` overrides, and `checkGuideMinimum`. If `build.ts` stopped passing `'persist'`, this test would still pass. The only guard on the real wiring is the mocked argument assertion at `build.test.ts:227`. Either drive the command through the commander program, or rename the test so it doesn't claim to cover the CLI path.

findings.title: `services/` and `adoption/` import each other's internals
findings.description: `ContextIntegrator.ts:9-10` says the `adoption/contracts.ts` import exists to keep the two directories from importing each other's internals. The resolver imports three services internals (`ContextProfileParser`, `promptFilePath`, `SystemPromptParser`), and `CoreServiceFactory.ts:12` imports the resolver back. I found no module cycle in the files I read, so this is a layering smell, not a bug. Consider moving the guide check into a module both sides can import.

findings.title: Positional parameters grow and literal values repeat
findings.description: `generateContext` now takes five positional parameters, with a `'persist' | 'read-only'` literal in second position, so call sites read `generateContext(resolvedId, 'persist', ...)` (line 202). The TypeScript rules call for an options object at three or more parameters. The `ContextIntegrator` constructor is now seven positional parameters (`ContextIntegrator.ts:86-94`).

findings.title: Adoption-state literals and the remedy text are repeated
findings.description: `'in_progress'`, `'complete'`, and `'declined'` appear as comparison literals here, as a write argument at `adoptionResolver.ts:88`, and in output text at `adoptionFacts.ts:44-46`. The `as const` list in `ConfigKeys.ts:28` makes a typo a compile error, but CLAUDE.md asks for one definition. The decline remedy is written twice, as `DECLINE_REMEDY` (`adoptionResolver.ts:28`) and inline at `adoptionFacts.ts:93`, with different formatting.

findings.title: No `projectPath` returns the concept prompt silently
findings.description: The guard `this.resolveAdoptionFn && project.projectPath && checkoutPath` skips adoption when `projectPath` is missing, and the concept prompt comes back. The CLI (`build.ts:51-56`) and MCP (`contextTools.ts:74-78`) both check it first, so production paths can't reach this. It is still a silent fallback to the exact prompt the feature exists to avoid. Throw an `AdoptionError` here instead.

findings.title: `ContextIntegrator.ts` is 398 lines and grows further
findings.description: CLAUDE.md asks for source files around 300 lines where practical. This diff adds about 20 lines to a file already over that. The adoption wiring could move into a helper beside the other resolvers.

findings.title: Guide check returns null with no fallback
findings.description: `SystemPromptParser.getPromptForInstruction` returns `match || null` (`SystemPromptParser.ts:211`), and matching is a substring test on `brownfield-adoption`, so an unrelated prompt doesn't satisfy it. The guard runs before `persistInProgress`, so a guide missing the prompt does not leave `in_progress` behind.

findings.title: Browser entry does not reach the adoption resolver
findings.description: `index.ts` re-exports `services/index.js`, which exports only `ContextIntegrator` (`services/index.ts:16`). That imports `adoption/contracts.ts`, which has no imports. `adoption/` is exported only from `node.ts:61`, so the `fs`-dependent resolver stays out of the browser bundle.
